name: Push, then pop
expr: (lambda H: [getattr(H, op[0])(*op[1:]) for op in args[0]])(MinHeap())
show: push 5, 3, 8, 1; then pop four times (push returns None)
why: pop always returns the smallest value left: 1, 3, 5, 8.

name: peek and len
expr: (lambda H: [getattr(H, op[0])(*op[1:]) for op in args[0]])(MinHeap())
show: push 4, 2; peek; len(h); pop; len(h); peek
why: peek returns the smallest without removing it: [None, None, 2, 2, 2, 1, 4].

name: Repeated values
expr: (lambda H: [getattr(H, op[0])(*op[1:]) for op in args[0]])(MinHeap())
why: Equal values are fine in a heap: 1, 2, 2, 2. A parent only has to be no bigger than its children.

name: Pushes and pops mixed
expr: (lambda H: [getattr(H, op[0])(*op[1:]) for op in args[0]])(MinHeap())
show: push 9, 4; pop; push 7, 1, 6; pop; pop; push 0; peek; len(h)
why: [None, None, 4, None, None, None, 1, 6, None, 0, 3]. If a later pop is wrong, an earlier pop may have left the list out of heap order: after moving the last value to the top, sift it down to the smaller child each time.

name: Heap sort
expr: (lambda H: (lambda xs: [[H.push(x) for x in xs], [H.pop() for _ in xs]][1])(args[0]))(MinHeap()) == sorted(args[0])
show: push 100 values in a mixed order, pop them all: sorted?
why: Popping everything gives the values in increasing order (this is heap sort, SORT-4).

name: Comparisons
expr: (lambda H: (lambda xs: [[H.push(x) for x in xs], (lambda out: [out == sorted(args[0]), comparisons() <= 4 * len(xs) * __import__('math').log2(len(xs))])(plain([H.pop() for _ in xs]))][1])(counted(args[0])))(MinHeap())
show: push 5,000 values from 5,000 down to 1, then pop them all: [sorted?, at most 4 n log₂ n comparisons?]
why: Each push and pop should compare only along one path of the tree: O(log n) comparisons. Finding the smallest with min() or a scan of the list costs n comparisons per pop, about 12.5 million here.

name: 30,000 values
expr: (lambda H: (lambda xs: [[H.push(x) for x in xs], (lambda out: [out[:5], out[-1], all(out[i] <= out[i + 1] for i in range(len(out) - 1))])([H.pop() for _ in xs])][1])(args[0]))(MinHeap())
show: push 30,000 values, then pop them all: [first five, last, in order?]
why: 60,000 operations at O(log n) each. If this timed out, look for list.insert, list.pop(0), sorting, or a scan of the whole list inside push or pop.
